q8.answer: The older run ends quietly as superseded. Under the production lock it reads /deploy/production/current_tag. If its SHA is not a descendant of that tag, it releases the lock and ends with no announcement. The staging lock has the same check. Its approval request just goes stale, and approving it is harmless.

q9.answer: Outside the window, the run waits and re-checks every 5 minutes until the window opens. Approving after hours only queues it. If another production deploy is running, it queues on the production-deploy lock. After getting the lock it re-checks the window, because the wait may have passed 15:00, and releases the lock and goes back to waiting if it has. It then runs the supersede check.

q10.answer: The canary's 1-minute 5xx ratio is measured, using the Prometheus query from environments.md. The pipeline polls Prometheus every 30 s for 15 min, starting when deploy.sh canary returns. Samples in the first 60 s are ignored. Any single sample above 1% fails the run, and so does empty or unreachable data after warm-up. A failure triggers canary-off, an announcement and the end of the run.

q11.answer: I did not decide this. The document says only that a manual approval job exists, that CI records who approved and when, and that #deploys gets failures, expiries and finished deploys. It does not say that a waiting run is announced to approvers. It does not say what information an approver is shown (SHA, staging smoke results, diff, migrations). The approval box does not specify this either. This is a gap.

q12.answer: It is not returned automatically. If a stable rollout fails in staging or in the production stable roll, deploy.sh has not yet written the tags. previous_tag would therefore point two versions back, so an automatic rollback could go to the wrong image. The pipeline stops, removes the canary in production, announces the failure and leaves a human to decide. Rollback is automatic only after staging smoke tests fail, when the deploy had succeeded and previous_tag is correct.
